speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if the skin lesions are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The recent history of self-resolving knee pain followed by wrist pain, combined with your camping trip in Minnesota and sexual activity, is concerning. Was the knee joint warm or swollen at the time, and do you have a specific type of rash, such as a "bull's-eye" lesion, anywhere on your body? REQUEST IMAGES: Request for photos of the wrist and any skin lesions.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cat Scratch Disease with Regional Lymphadenitis and Reactive Arthritis. The specific description of "painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions" on the extremities, combined with wrist swelling, recent travel to Minnesota (tick exposure), and a preceding episode of monoarticular knee pain, is highly suggestive of Bartonella henselae infection. While Lyme disease is a differential given the geographic history, the lesion morphology points strongly toward Cat Scratch Disease. I am confident in this diagnosis based on the clinical presentation.
